subject: english-literature
title: Genres in Dialogue
welcome_lead: Genres are not boxes but ongoing conversations. Each new work reshapes the genre's possibilities.
meta_desc: English Literature: genre theory, hybridity, and intertextual dialogue between forms.
final_note: Genres breathe — they expand each time a writer enters them.

concepts.def: A category of text defined by shared formal and thematic conventions.
The mixing of two or more genres within a single text.
A recurring feature that signals genre to readers.
Undermining or rewriting a genre's conventions.
Jauss's term for the prior assumptions a reader brings to a text.
Fiction that draws attention to its own status as fiction.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cloud Atlas by David Mitchell shuttles between thriller, historical fiction, dystopia and post-apocalyptic narrative. The hybridity is the point — genres mirror each other.
Angela Carter's The Bloody Chamber rewrites fairy tales, granting female protagonists agency where the originals had passivity. Subversion exposes the politics of convention.
When a narrator addresses the reader directly or comments on the act of writing, you have metafiction. Italo Calvino's If on a winter's night a traveler is built from this device.

numericals.q: How many genres mix in a hybrid like Cloud Atlas (at least)?

free_texts.q: What term describes fiction that comments on its own status? (one word)
